A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bolt3D and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bolt3D reconstruction results, inference timings, geometry-autoencoder evaluations and supplementary ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds FID measurements and a quantitative and qualitative comparison with MVSplat360.

M1.justification: The diffusion model, geometry VAE, Gaussian head and inference procedure are retained. The new synthetic foreground-masking and binary-cross-entropy paragraph in Section 8.2 supplies implementation details without establishing that the method was revised.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation datasets and tasks are retained. The new MVSplat360 comparison uses the existing two- and four-view DL3DV coverage; low-overlap scenarios and six-view DL3DV evaluation already appear in v1.

E2.justification: MVSplat360, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Section 7.2, Table 5 and Figure 8. Existing regression, generative and optimization-based comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID alongside PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS in Tables 1–3. The new MVSplat360 experiment specifies resolution matching and evaluation cropping. Existing training budgets and evaluation protocols are retained; Section 10 clarifies existing DL3DV selections rather than reporting a changed split.

E4.justification: New Figure 8 examines MVSplat360's conditioning failure when input views have little or no overlap. Existing geometry-VAE and Gaussian-head ablations, normalization analysis, and resolution/FOV comparisons remain unchanged, with supplementary tables renumbered.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Adding FID changes the evaluation metrics, not uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: FID results substantially extend Tables 1–3 and reveal metric-dependent rankings: LatentSplat beats Bolt3D on FID, including 2.79 versus 3.66 on two-view RE10K. New Table 5 reports MVSplat360/Bolt3D PSNR of 13.97/17.75 for two-view DL3DV and 15.42/20.64 for four-view DL3DV. Existing main-table PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS values and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations (1)–(9), geometry normalization and loss derivations are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central representation, fast generation and up-to-300× inference-cost claims. Section 9 newly asserts that Bolt3D is the first work to explore Geometry VAE architecture and training recipes, modestly strengthening its novelty claim.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 qualifies superiority over LatentSplat to image-level metrics and hypothesizes an adversarial-training explanation for its FID advantage. Expanded Section 9 discusses pointmaps versus depth, attributes CAT3D's quality advantage to greater view coverage, and explicitly identifies static-only generation. Earlier limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 8.2 newly documents foreground-only reconstruction loss and alpha-mask supervision for synthetic data. New Section 10 lists the 16 DL3DV evaluation scenes and exact conditioning-frame indices for two-, four- and six-view setups. These improve reproducibility without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens coverage of reconstruction, video generation and native 3D latent models. Section 2 explicitly positions Bolt3D's view-centric representation against scene models including SCube, NeuralField-LDM and Prometheus, emphasizing autoencoder limitations. Section 9 additionally relates future directions to Geo4D, VGGT and CAT4D.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of related work and experimental discussion, revised acknowledgments and funding information, and new supplementary subsections. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 gain FID columns, Table 2 reorders the CO3D categories, and Figure 6 is reformatted. v2 adds the MVSplat360 table and qualitative figure; existing supplementary tables and the Gaussian-head diagram are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation balance by reporting FID disadvantages and qualifying the LatentSplat comparison, while adding a relevant comparator and useful reproducibility details. These gains are limited by an unresolved timing claim: Table 5 says MVSplat360 is over 200× slower, whereas Section 7.2 gives 5.8 minutes versus 7 seconds, approximately 50×, without explaining another cost basis. Overall, the added transparency and evidence provide an incremental quality improvement.
